feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen impact with clearer outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear seniority and progression: the move from coordinator to director to consultant is logical and strengthens credibility.  
- Strong domain positioning: public-sector digital platforms, governance, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across sections: “core competencies,” “topline skills,” “technical + IT,” and “recent projects” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role and earlier positions; quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or performance where possible.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use either “AI-enabled” or “AI enabled” consistently; standardize punctuation around lists and hyphenation (e.g., “organization-wide,” “front-end”). No major misspellings found, but “livestreams”/“Livestream studio workflows” may read inconsistently depending on whether “Livestream” is a brand reference.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise positioning statement plus one impact-oriented sentence; reduce the long list of functions.
- Add a concrete scope cue from recent work, e.g. “enterprise web modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector platforms” or “high-volume, mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “Leads” with “Leading” or make both sentences parallel in tense/style.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Combines digital strategy, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems and multimedia production to improve how mission-driven institutions publish, measure and scale user-focused communications, including AI-enabled experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The long capability list duplicates Topline Skills; keep the intro more positioning-focused.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with Topline Skills and the header. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use sharper, leadership-oriented wording and reduce generic terms like “operations” where possible.
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and workflow/platform integration.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- Keep style consistent by avoiding mixed constructions (“communications operations” vs. “livestream operations”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This block substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making it more concise or more executive-level.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps closely with both Work Experience and the Multimedia/Technical sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement-focused bullet rather than paragraph-style text.
- Use parallel verbs and cleaner phrasing: “Created AI-powered legislative search using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Replace vague wording like “designed for continued campaign growth” with sharper language such as “built on a modular architecture to support future campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot,” keep capitalization consistent, and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing it more if this section is kept.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + hands-on scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the projects section and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this level.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client scope: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations.”
- Consolidate bullets to 4–5 and lead with strongest differentiators: enterprise web improvement, Drupal campaign builds, analytics/workflow systems, and AI-enabled search.
- Replace generic phrases like “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with stronger verbs: “led,” “built,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “defined.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search accuracy/adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and “campaign/microsite” work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- Governance, analytics, and cross-channel operations also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting scope and new technical execution.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It can be sharper by reducing channel-overview language, foregrounding the biggest outcomes, and avoiding overlap with earlier NACo roles on newsletters/video.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope-and-impact line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the website modernization as the lead bullet and make the outcome more active: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen results language in other bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video content.”
- If possible, add measurable outcomes for analytics/governance: reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, publishing efficiency, reduced bottlenecks, or improved decision-making cadence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry on newsletters/social; either add stronger outcomes here or trim.
- Video-program language also overlaps with prior NACo roles; keep this item focused on studio buildout and enterprise leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level: editorial operations, newsletter ownership, and establishing repeatable advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director role; use “day-to-day operations” or “owned execution” to differentiate.
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/operationalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and audience/governance strengths rather than repeating generic digital terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital leadership
- Editorial governance and publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications strategy
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and content strategy
- Use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more current, concise feel.
- Swap “messaging” for “communications” to better match the leadership level shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, consider “Audience strategy and content planning” to sound more strategic and less tactical.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats language already established in the header and recent NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skills, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. It should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and implementation themes that support the recent Drupal modernization and AI search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-signal or older platforms unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first, as it is most supported by recent experience.
- Cut “jQuery” unless specifically required by the job; it dates the profile and adds little strategic value.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current platform/tool list duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeat Core Competencies; keep wording distinct here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and business impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding across GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Put the most strategic items first: “Analytics strategy” or “Measurement & optimization” before platforms.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “C-suite dashboards” for clearer, more standard phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “for enterprise web performance and content decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every platform here if they are already listed elsewhere; this section should signal senior-level strengths, not inventory tools.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it tighter, more senior, and oriented to delivery capability rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations
- Virtual event technical direction and run-of-show execution
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier such as “broadcast-quality,” “end-to-end,” or “multi-camera” to signal level.
- Keep to 4 bullets max; avoid software/tool detail here since Technical + IT already covers creative tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is partly duplicated by “Multimedia & Creative Tools” and several work-experience bullets.
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies; use “livestream and hybrid event production” to consolidate.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add level/context instead of just names: “Drupal site building and modernization • WordPress • SharePoint intranets • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it is less central than Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint for this CV.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “CMS & Web Platforms” may read more naturally than “Web Platforms & CMS.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” under Topline Skills, which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- If both sections stay, use Topline Skills for strategic capability and this section for tools only, or consolidate them.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should be tighter, more current, and framed around implementation strengths that support recent Drupal, analytics, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter, grouped list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value and date the entry.
- If space allows, add a brief qualifier for impact: “Front-end implementation, tagging, lightweight serverless scripting, and deployment automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or differentiate this item as hands-on tools only.
- Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions are useful differentiators here—keep those, since they add more specificity than the repeated basics.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Systems.”
- Group by function for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Keep only tools you’ve used recently or materially; consider dropping older/lower-signal items like Basecamp or Trello if space is tight.
- If possible, connect this category to outcomes elsewhere in experience bullets (e.g., automated reporting, editorial workflows, cross-team planning) rather than expanding the list here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and automation themes already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them too prominently in multiple sections.
- Slack and Teams are low-differentiation tools; include only if collaboration platforms are genuinely important to target roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since the CV already shows strong email leadership in recent NACo roles, this item should be tighter and framed around enterprise/member communications rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Replace with: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If space allows, add light context: Enterprise email automation • Member communications • Newsletter operations
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was minimal or older, drop it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about newsletters/email; avoid adding descriptive claims here that repeat those entries
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider listing only Higher Logic + Dynamics 365 and removing Mailchimp unless it was used substantially

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and misses a chance to signal level of use or business impact. Tighten it into a more capability-led, less repetitive line.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI • Analytics architecture & KPI reporting • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing) • Executive dashboarding
- Replace vague nouns like “Dashboarding” with outcome-oriented phrasing such as “executive dashboarding” or “KPI reporting.”
- Group tools first, then capabilities; this reads more senior and aligns with your recent NACo/consulting work.
- If space allows elsewhere, quantify impact in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., reporting for 3.5M annual page views or org-wide decision support.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one section or making this one tools-only.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are broader practices, not IT tools; they may fit better under competencies than Technical + IT.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, not generic support: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience/reach, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the second sentence to foreground hands-on delivery: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, name tools/platforms or ownership areas to show capability: CMS publishing, video production, livestream operations, editorial coordination.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update”; differentiate this as the launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in 2018–2024 roles; use “helped establish” or “formalized early processes” instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation/program support and the first-podcast launch.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast the anchor: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add scope or results: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects delivered.
- Consider a two-bullet format for clarity:
- Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast; led concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production, while contributing digital and multimedia content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video or digital operations here; those are better established in 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Make it a tighter software/tools list and avoid repeating production capabilities already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Replace with: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want one capability phrase, keep only one concise addition: Broadcast/livestream production tools
